input.subject: 27 Thistle Lane – bedroom radiator (ref R/12): your decision needed
input.body:
Dear Landlord,

Re: 27 Thistle Lane, Brackley Vale, ZZ3 9ZZ – bedroom radiator not heating (ref R/12)

Thank you for approving the repair with Harlow Heating up to £150. Unfortunately we can't proceed within those terms:

- Harlow Heating have told us they are fully booked until 3 November. They could attend sooner as an emergency visit, but at double their normal rate, which they haven't priced; it would likely exceed your £150 limit.
- Another firm, Quick Fix Heating, has offered to attend on Monday 6 October and quoted £230 including parts for a radiator inspection and valve replacement. That is £80 above your limit and not your chosen contractor.

The rest of the house is heating normally; only the bedroom is affected and the tenant reports the room is very cold.

Please reply with the option you would like:
1. Wait for Harlow Heating's first standard slot (from 3 November), within £150.
2. Ask Harlow Heating for a price for an earlier emergency visit, which we will bring back to you before booking.
3. Approve Quick Fix Heating at £230 for attendance on 6 October.

We won't book anything until we hear from you.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance Team

input.subject: 27 Thistle Lane – bedroom radiator (ref R/12) update
input.body:
Dear Tenant,

Re: 27 Thistle Lane, Brackley Vale, ZZ3 9ZZ – bedroom radiator (ref R/12)

Thank you for reporting this. Our landlord's chosen heating engineer has limited availability, so we have gone back to the landlord with options for getting someone out. We have asked for a decision and will update you by 6 October at the latest.

In the meantime, a few safe checks that sometimes fix a cold radiator:
- Make sure the valve(s) at either end of the radiator are turned fully open (the numbered thermostatic head turned to its highest setting).
- If you have a radiator key and feel comfortable, with the heating switched off and the radiator cool, you can bleed it: hold a cloth under the bleed valve at the top corner and open it slowly until water appears, then close it. Check the boiler pressure afterwards and let us know if it has dropped.
Please don't attempt anything beyond this.

If anyone in the household is elderly, unwell, very young or otherwise vulnerable to the cold, please let us know straight away so we can prioritise accordingly. If these checks fix the radiator, please tell us too.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance Team
